delivered:
Mitigation proposal: Establish a closed-loop “screw-recovery/weight drift” control using only existing sensors (barrel thermocouples, cycle-time logger, and check-weigher). Mechanism: Treat the increasing screw recovery time and part weight drift as an indicator of degraded melt density/consistency and inconsistent back-off behavior; use the check-weigher output at the quality gate and the cycle-time logger’s recovery-time trend to detect drift, and automatically adjust the injection hold time/pressure setpoint and/or back-off speed to bring part weight back to target within the same barrel setpoints. 

DIRECTION-OF-EFFECT: The driving variable is the deviation of part weight from target. A positive deviation (part weight > target) indicates excessive shot volume, which is corrected by a negative directional adjustment to the back-off speed setpoint (reduce back-off speed to ensure more complete metering and prevent over-accumulation) and a positive directional adjustment to injection hold pressure (increase hold pressure slightly to stabilize melt density and prevent compression-induced weight loss or inconsistency). Conversely, a negative deviation would trigger opposite adjustments, but the current failure mode is positive drift. The physical mechanism is that reduced back-off speed increases the consistency of the metered shot, while increased hold pressure compensates for density variations, together reducing the variability and mean of part weight.

Implementation: 1) From the check-weigher, compute rolling average part weight and deviation from target; 2) From the cycle-time logger, compute rolling average screw recovery time and detect increases beyond a threshold; 3) When both conditions persist for a defined window, trigger a corrective action: reduce the back-off speed (to ensure more complete metering) and/or increase injection hold pressure slightly to stabilize density, while keeping barrel temperature setpoints unchanged; 4) Log the adjustments and verify with subsequent check-weigher readings that weight returns to target and recovery time stabilizes. Measures relied on: Existing sensors only—barrel thermocouples (to confirm no temperature drift is causing the issue), cycle-time logger (for recovery time monitoring), and check-weigher (for part weight feedback). No new instrumentation is added; the mitigation uses data fusion from these existing measurements to implement a simple feedback correction to process parameters (back-off speed/hold pressure) that affects part weight and screw recovery consistency.

IMPLEMENTATION BILL:
- Sensor Inputs:
  - Check-weigher: Provides direct measurement of part weight (mass) at the quality gate. Used to compute rolling average part weight and deviation from target.
  - Cycle-time logger: Provides direct measurement of cycle time components, specifically screw recovery time. Used to compute rolling average screw recovery time and detect increases.
  - Barrel zone thermocouples: Provide direct measurement of barrel temperature in each zone. Used to confirm no temperature drift is causing the issue (i.e., temperatures are within specified setpoints).
- Derived Quantities:
  - Rolling average part weight: Computed as the mean of the last N check-weigher measurements, where N is a defined window (e.g., 5 cycles).
  - Deviation from target: Computed as (rolling average part weight - target part weight).
  - Rolling average screw recovery time: Computed as the mean of the last N cycle-time logger measurements for the recovery phase, where N is the same window as above.
  - Recovery time increase threshold: Pre-defined value; if rolling average screw recovery time exceeds this threshold, the condition is flagged.
- Control Actions:
  - Adjustment to back-off speed setpoint: Derived from the sign and magnitude of the deviation from target part weight. For positive deviation, apply a negative step change (reduce speed) proportional to deviation.
  - Adjustment to injection hold pressure setpoint: Derived from the sign and magnitude of the deviation from target part weight. For positive deviation, apply a positive step change (increase pressure) proportional to deviation.
- Verification:
  - Post-adjustment check-weigher readings are monitored to confirm that part weight returns to within target tolerance and that screw recovery time stabilizes.
